advances: Actual compact convex families with a common homothetic shape, a terminating forest of exact midpoint identities and a full star at one root.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The midpoint identity on a forest edge gives $r_{F(p)}=(r_p+r_{v_c})/2$ and $a_{F(p)}=(a_p+a_{v_c})/2$. Indeed the Minkowski midpoint of two positive homothets of the common convex shape is the homothet with those averaged parameters. Its scale is determined by any directional width of the body divided by the positive width of $K$ in that direction, and its translation by the centroid. Rewriting each equation from parent to child and using termination puts all bases in the affine hull of the roots. The pairs $v_c,2p_*-v_c$ have a centrally symmetric hull spanning that same affine space. Hence $p_*$ is in the relative interior of $\operatorname{conv}P$. In rank zero the conclusion is immediate.

Replace $C$ by the convex hull of its finitely many positive sampled fibers. This compact hull is contained in $C$ and contains every original positive integer fiber, so they are unchanged. It has a nonempty compact fiber at every base of $\operatorname{conv}P$. For any nonzero continuous direction $u$, its fiber support value $H_u(z)=h_{C_z}(u)$ is a finite concave function there: convexity of the ambient hull gives Minkowski containment between interpolated fibers. At the relative-interior point $p_*$ it has an affine supporting majorant $m_u$, by the supporting hyperplane theorem for a finite concave function on its relative domain. The exact midpoint star gives $H_u(q_c)+H_u(v_c)=2H_u(p_*)$ for every pair. The corresponding two nonnegative gaps under $m_u$ sum to zero because $m_u$ is affine and tight at $p_*$. Thus $m_u(v_c)=h_{K_{v_c}}(u)$ at every root.

Choose a nonzero $u$ and its negative. The affine function $\ell_r=(m_u+m_{-u})/(h_K(u)+h_K(-u))$ agrees with the radius at each root by the homothetic support formula. The denominator is strictly positive since $K$ is full-dimensional. For each coordinate direction $e_j$, the affine function $m_{e_j}-h_K(e_j)\ell_r$ agrees with coordinate $j$ of the true centroid at each root. These coordinate functions define $A$. Both affine identities propagate backward from the roots along every forest edge because the same midpoint equations hold for affine data and for the given data. The graph formula follows.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex with nonempty positive-volume integer fiber support $P$, $d\ge1$. Suppose each positive fiber is $K_p=a_p+r_pK$, where $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is one full-dimensional convex body with centroid zero and $r_p>0$. Suppose that a terminating forest on $P$ has roots $v_1,\ldots,v_J$. For each nonroot $p$, its parent $F(p)$ and an associated root $v_c$ satisfy $F(p)=(p+v_c)/2$ and $K_{F(p)}=(K_p+K_{v_c})/2$. Suppose a designated root $p_*$ has a full exact midpoint star: for every other root $v_c$, the base $q_c=2p_*-v_c$ lies in $P$ and $K_{p_*}=(K_{q_c}+K_{v_c})/2$.

Then there exist an affine function $\ell_r$ and an affine map $A$ on $\operatorname{aff}P$ with $r_p=\ell_r(p)$ and $a_p=A(p)$ for every $p\in P$. In particular the true centroid graph is an affine copy of $P$ under $p\mapsto(p,A(p))$.
title: An exact root-midpoint star forces affine homothetic fiber data
